question.value: Determine the millimetre-wave rotational spectrum of 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal in the laboratory and search for this molecule (and related aldehydes) towards the solar-type protostar IRAS16293-2422 and the high-mass star-forming region Sgr B2(N).

evidence.quote: The aim of this work is to deepen knowledge about the millimetre-wave spectrum of 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal in the region enabling its detailed search towards astronomical objects. In particular, we target the solar-type protostar IRAS16293–2422 and star-forming region Sagittarius (Sgr) B2(N).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00074.S and ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00278.S.

evidence.quote: We provide laboratory analysis of hundreds of rotational transitions of 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal in the ground state and the lowest lying excited vibrational state.
In order to search for 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal, CH$_2$C(OH)CHO, toward Sgr B2(N1S), we relied on the LTE parameters derived for acetaldehyde

We also report in Table [\[t:coldens\]](#t:coldens) the column density upper limits that we obtained with the ReMoCA survey for two related aldehydes: the more saturated molecule 2-hydroxypropanal, CH$_3$CH(OH)CHO and 3-hydroxypropenal, HOCHCHCHO

We also report in Table [\[t:coldens\]](#t:coldens) the column density upper limits that we obtained with the ReMoCA survey for two related aldehydes: the more saturated molecule 2-hydroxypropanal, CH$_3$CH(OH)CHO and 3-hydroxypropenal, HOCHCHCHO
The high spatial resolution of $\sim$0.5$\ensuremath{''}$ clearly disentangles the emission of the two components A and B, which are separated by $\sim$5$\ensuremath{''}$.

analysis_steps.goal: Quantum-chemical calculations and laboratory rotational spectroscopy of 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal

method.value: Record millimetre-wave spectrum (128-166 GHz and 285-329 GHz), perform DFT B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p) calculations, assign transitions using Loomis-Wood plots, fit spectroscopic constants using Watson's A-reduced Hamiltonian in I^r representation, and compute rotational and vibrational partition functions.

evidence.quote: we have performed quantum-chemical calculations employing the density functional theory (DFT) combined with the B3LYP functional and Pople’s basis set with added polarization and diffusion functions (6-311++G(d,p)).
The Pickett’s program package SPFIT/SPCAT (cite: PICKETT1991) with Watson’s $A$-reduced Hamiltonian in I$^{\text{r}}$ representation were employed throughout the analysis.
The rotational partition functions for different temperatures were obtained from SPCAT covering all rotational states up to $J$ = 100.

key_parameters.value: Frequency ranges: 128-166 GHz and 285-329 GHz; J up to 100 for Q_rot

evidence.quote: The spectrum of 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal was recorded with the upgraded Prague semiconductor millimetre-wave spectrometer described elsewhere (cite: Kania2006) in two spectral ranges (128–166 GHz and 285–329 GHz).
The rotational partition functions for different temperatures were obtained from SPCAT covering all rotational states up to $J$ = 100.

evidence.quote: A total number of 669 and 295 distinct frequency lines covering 968 and 487 rotational transitions was used in the assignment of the ground and excited vibrational states, respectively.

claims.hypothesis: Accurate millimetre-wave spectroscopic constants of 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal can be determined up to 329 GHz to enable reliable astronomical searches in ALMA spectral surveys.
claims.experiment: Measured the rotational spectrum of 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal between 128-166 GHz and 285-329 GHz and fitted 968 ground-state and 487 v21=1 transitions using Watson's A-reduced Hamiltonian.
claims.result: Rotational and quartic centrifugal distortion constants were improved by up to three orders of magnitude, and sextic constants and v21=1 constants were determined for the first time.
claims.finding: The new laboratory measurements significantly improve upon previous microwave data and provide accurate frequency predictions for interstellar searches.

evidence.quote: All constants were improved by up to three orders of magnitude and a set of sextic centrifugal distortion constants is determined for the first time.
These new laboratory measurements provided accurate frequency predictions to search for the molecule toward IRAS16293 B and Sgr B2(N).

claims.hypothesis: 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal is detectable towards IRAS16293 B, where chemical models predict it to be ~1.4 times more abundant than its isomer 3-hydroxypropenal (6.6e-4 relative to CH3OH).
claims.experiment: Searched for 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal in the ALMA PILS survey spectrum of IRAS16293 B using LTE modeling in CASSIS at T_ex = 125 K and 300 K.
claims.result: Nondetection of 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal with 3-sigma column density upper limits of 9.4e14 cm^-2 (125 K) and 2.4e15 cm^-2 (300 K), corresponding to <= 2.4e-4 relative to CH3OH and an isomer ratio <= 0.9-1.3.
claims.finding: 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal is not detected in IRAS16293 B, though the upper limits remain consistent with the chemical model predictions within the factor of 20 model uncertainty.

evidence.quote: The upper limit on its abundance with respect to CH$_3$OH is consequently about $\sim$2.4 $\times$ 10$^{-4}$, that is a factor of about 3 lower than the predictions of the chemical model, but still within the uncertainties.
The 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal/3-hydroxypropenal abundance ratio is estimated to be $\lesssim$ 0.9-1.3 in agreement with the predicted value of $\sim$ 1.4.

claims.hypothesis: 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal and related C3 aldehydes (2-hydroxypropanal and 3-hydroxypropenal) are present in the hot molecular core Sgr B2(N1).
claims.experiment: Searched the ALMA ReMoCA spectral line survey towards Sgr B2(N1S) using LTE synthetic spectra generated with Weeds adopting the physical parameters of acetaldehyde.
claims.result: None of the three molecules were detected, yielding column density upper limits of < 7.2e16 cm^-2 (2-hydroxyprop-2-enal), < 1.7e17 cm^-2 (2-hydroxypropanal), and < 7.0e16 cm^-2 (3-hydroxypropenal).
claims.finding: 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal, 2-hydroxypropanal, and 3-hydroxypropenal are at least 9, 4, and 10 times less abundant than acetaldehyde in Sgr B2(N1S).

evidence.quote: We also report the nondetection of 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal toward the hot molecular core Sgr B2(N1). We did not detect the related aldehydes 2-hydroxypropanal and 3-hydroxypropenal either. We find that these three molecules are at least 9, 4, and 10 times less abundant than acetaldehyde in this source, respectively.

why_this_data.value: Previous microwave predictions below 25 GHz were unreliable when extrapolated to ALMA frequencies; PILS and ReMoCA provide high-sensitivity, high-angular-resolution unbiased spectral surveys of prime astrochemical targets where related isomers (like 3-hydroxypropenal in PILS) were studied.

evidence.quote: The predictions of the rotational transitions to the frequency range of common surveys, such as surveys performed with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), like the Re-Exploring Molecular Complexity with ALMA survey (ReMoCA) that covers the frequency range 84–114 GHz (cite: Belloche19) or the Protostellar Interferometric Line Survey (PILS) covering 329–363 GHz (cite: Jorgensen2016), are rather unreliable if they are based on low-frequency data.
Thanks to its high sensitivity (rms $\sim$ 4-5 mJy in a bin of 1 km s$^{-1}$), a large variety of species were detected for the first time in low-mass protostars through this survey

why_this_method.value: Selected the offset position Sgr B2(N1S) because it has lower continuum opacity than the hot core peak, and used LTE synthetic modeling justified by the high gas densities of the hot core.

evidence.loc: Search for 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal and related aldehydes toward Sgr B2(N1) - Observations
evidence.quote: It has a lower continuum opacity compared to the peak of the hot core which facilitates the detection of spectral lines of molecules.

evidence.loc: Search for 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal and related aldehydes toward Sgr B2(N1) - Observations
evidence.quote: The high densities of the regions where hot-core emission is detected in Sgr B2(N) (cite: Bonfand19) justify our assumption of LTE.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using glyceraldehyde instead of dihydroxyacetone as the chemical precursor for in situ synthesis of 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal (dihydroxyacetone was chosen as more cost-effective).

evidence.quote: Either of them proved to be a good source for producing the desired species in our experiment. Dihydroxyacetone as a precursor turned out to be a cost-effective solution, and therefore, all further measurements were carried out with it.

limitations_admitted.value: Insufficient line intensities prevented the analysis of other low-lying excited vibrational states of 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal, hampering assessment of possible Coriolis or Fermi interactions with the v15 state at 277.4 cm^-1.

evidence.quote: However, the possible interaction with the nearby excited vibrational state at 277.4 cm$^{-1}$, or even a combination of both effects cannot be excluded either. Unfortunately, the insufficient intensities for other low-lying vibrational states made their analysis impossible, thus hampering further assessment of this issue.

limitations_admitted.value: Lines of 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal in IRAS16293 B at 125 K are mostly blended with transitions of other species.

evidence.quote: For 125 K, which was slightly favoured for 3-hydroxypropenal (cite: Coutens2022), the lines of 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal are usually blended with other species.

limitations_admitted.value: Large uncertainties (factor of 20) in the chemical network predictions for 2-hydroxyprop-2-enal production and destruction.

evidence.quote: The derived abundance is still within the uncertainties of the chemical model which is estimated to be a factor 20 for this species.

referee_caveats_inferred: Upper limits in Sgr B2(N1S) and IRAS16293 B rely on subjective visual inspection or unspecified single-line criteria in crowded spectra rather than automated statistical fitting across all transitions.
Assuming identical source size, temperature, and linewidth as acetaldehyde in Sgr B2(N1S) may introduce systematic bias if C3 hydroxy-aldehydes trace a more compact or cooler sub-region.

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA interferometric data are available in the ALMA archive; laboratory measured transitions (Table 5) are available at CDS.

evidence.quote: The interferometric data are available in the ALMA archive at https://almascience.eso.org/aq/.
Table 5 is only available in electronic form at the CDS via anonymous ftp to cdsarc.u-strasbg.fr (130.79.128.5) or via http://cdsweb.u-strasbg.fr/cgi-bin/qcat?J/A+A/

missing_for_reproduction: Complete background LTE model of all previously identified molecules in Sgr B2(N1S) (shown as the green curve in Figs. 4-7) needed to evaluate line blending and upper limits.
Exact list of unblended transitions used to set the 3-sigma column density upper limits in IRAS16293 B.
Full self-calibration and continuum subtraction scripts for ReMoCA and PILS cubes if starting from raw archival visibilities.
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~1-5 TB for raw PILS and ReMoCA archival visibilities; a few MB for extracted 1D spectra at IRAS16293 B and Sgr B2(N1S) and CDS spectroscopic tables.
reproducibility.score_reason: Spectroscopic constants, partition functions, target coordinates, and LTE physical parameters (T_ex, FWHM, source size) are explicitly tabulated, and raw ALMA data plus CDS line lists are public. However, reproducing the exact upper limits requires the full multi-species background models and reduced 1D spectra from PILS and ReMoCA, and the specific transitions used for the IRAS16293 B upper limits are not listed.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The astronomical results are non-detections (upper limits) that depend on visual inspection of line blending against complex multi-species background models not fully provided with the paper.
